thread:
incident-bot: Pager: high-severity — smart-routing fallbacks showing KV cache reuse across model variants in eu-west-1. Auto-escalate to on-call. Tags: smart-routing, kv-cache, variant-misserve. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2065432109

Sara-b: I see customer reports that completions are returning outputs for the wrong model (e.g. response looks like gpt-2 style prompts from an Llama family test) — happening in eu-west-1. Error rate on routing metrics jumped ~12% at 22:03 UTC.

Nick-io: Confirmed. Traces show requests routed to fallback variant v1-quant but the KV prefix key used was for v2/fp16, so cached prefix tokens are being reused.

Mike-runtime: logs: ```[22:02:58 UTC] route_decision: primary=llama-70b-v2 region=eu-west-1 variant=v2-fp16 fallback=v1-quant cache_key=prefix:llama-70b-v2:shard-3 -> cache_hit=true value_variant=v1-quant``` That mismatch is the problem — cache keys don't include variant id in some cases.

Anjan: Impact summary from metrics: ~1200 impacted requests/min at peak, affecting both hosted customers and a few Dedicated clusters that use shared KV namespacing. CS reported 4 paying customers noticing semantic regressions in responses. Potential data exposure risk low, but correctness is impacted.

Sara-b: Immediate mitigation steps proposed: 1) disable smart-routing fallback to force primary model only for eu-west-1 (quick config flip). 2) invalidate KV namespace for model-prefixes in eu-west-1 to prevent misserve. 3) create a canary routing policy that includes variant id in cache key — will require a small runtime patch.

Nick-io: I'm on the disable step. Running: ```curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/routing/policies/disable" -d '{"policy":"smart-fallback-eu-west-1"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN"``` -> status 202 accepted. (devex-bot: :eyes:)

devex-bot: deploy-bot: routing-policy-update queued on control-plane (job 78921). Expected propagate time ~15s.

Mike-runtime: Starting KV invalidate command: ```/usr/local/bin/kvctl invalidate --namespace=kv-prefix-eu-west --prefix="model:llama-70b" --confirm``` kicking now. Will stream logs.

(30s later) Mike-runtime: invalidate returned 204. Sampling post-invalidate traffic — cache hit rate for model prefixes dropped from 87% -> 5% (expected).

Anjan: What's the rollback plan if disabling smart-routing makes latency spike or capacity issues?

Sara-b: We will temporarily increase dedicated pool autoscale for eu-west-1 by +10% and enable burst capacity while fallback disabled. I've opened a capacity ticket to infra.

cs-rep: FYI, I've messaged affected customers with a short note: "We are investigating routing anomalies that may affect response correctness. We're mitigating and will follow up with incident summary." (added to support thread).

Nick-io: Observability: added a new temporary metric that emits (cache_key, resolved_variant, requested_variant) for mismatch sampling. Early data shows ~4.3% of cache hits are mismatched variant mapping within last 5m.

Sara-b: OK folks — current status: smart-fallback disabled (control-plane job succeeded), KV namespace invalidated, autoscale bump in progress. Impact: correctness reduced while mismatch present, but mitigation should stop further wrong serv es. Customer outreach in progress.

Mike-runtime: Starting a lightweight runtime patch branch to append variant id to cache key generation. Patch: ```diff --git a/runtime/cache.cc b/runtime/cache.cc index 123..456 --- a/runtime/cache.cc +++ b/runtime/cache.cc @@ -210,6 +210,8 @@ string make_cache_key(const Model& m, const Request& r) { - string key = "model:" + m.name + ":shard-" + to_string(r.shard); + // include variant id to avoid cross-variant reuse + key += ":variant-" + m.variant_id; + return key; }``` Will run through CI. If green we can roll to canary tomorrow.

Anjan: Please capture CI perf and latency before canary. Also need migration plan for existing cached entries (we already invalidated for prefix but some other namespaces might persist).

Nick-io: Creating incident ticket now: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2065432109 (owner: sara-b). Adding post-incident checklist.

Sara-b: Handoff: I'm staying on until 01:00 UTC. After that, Nick will take primary oncall for the overnight window. Nick, please monitor routing-mismatch-rate, cache-hit-by-variant, and customer escalations.

Nick-io: Taking handoff. Will keep this thread updated. Adding a brief runbook: 1) If mismatch rate > 1% for 10m, re-enable smart-fallback (if previously disabled) is NOT recommended — instead keep fallback disabled and escalate to runtime team to increase capacity. 2) If latency > 500ms p95 after autoscale, revert autoscale and open capacity incident.

devex-bot: note: triggered automated customer impact summarizer — draft: "~4 customers received degraded completions between 22:02–22:18 UTC in eu-west-1. We mitigated by disabling smart-fallback and invalidating cache. Root cause: cache key generation did not include variant identifier leading to cross-variant reuse."

Anjan: Recording timeline and evidence in incident ticket. Will attach sampled mismatched traces and affected request ids.

cs-rep: Customers asked for ETA on fix. Suggested reply: "We have a permanent fix in development and expect a canary rollout within 24 hours pending CI and perf validation. We'll update by EOD."

Sara-b: Thanks team. Next steps: patch in PR -> run perf CI -> canary tomorrow eu-west small % -> full rollout and postmortem. Leaving detailed notes in INC-2065432109.

Nick-io: (reaction) :thumbsup: 

incident-bot: Incident INC-2065432109 created; severity: Sev2; assignee: sara-b; status: mitigated (active monitoring).

Sara-b: Closing timeline note: last impacted request observed at 22:18 UTC after KV invalidate. Continuing to monitor for 2h then close follow-ups.

Nick-io: I'll post an interim incident summary for customers and product ops in #incidents-summary when stable.

(END of thread)
